title: R15b v3: gate/merge/executor integration — stale.py evidence in the gate, merged_at and changed_files stamped by merge(), gate stamps cleared on fix-round replies, allocation and active Jev routing hooks in executor.start, scout reuse check in spawn_scout
spec:
v3 after spec reviews T-0655 and T-0657 (executor.start derives the ready set and priorities itself; hooks live inside the branch that picks an executor; skipped-scout results are real findings). Why: merged pure modules need their call sites: daemon.stale_check/_record_stale_check/_stale_rebase (orchestrator/daemon.py:1152-1223 on goal/T-0561 after the R15a merge) only knows path signals; merge.merge (orchestrator/merge.py:25-99) stamps no merged_at (merge wait undefined for Planner merges, AP P0 gap) and no changed_files (stale.overlapping_merge floor); executor.post_tool_result with replace_result=True (executor.py:215-247) leaves pipeline.gated_at set so gate() skips a task fixed by codex_reply (Planner had to clear it by hand on T-0570/T-0574 today); executor.start (executor.py:249-300) picks executors without allocation or active Jev adjustment; mcp.spawn_scout (mcp.py:75-77) launches without the scout_evidence reuse check.
What. Tests: this repo runs unittest; every acceptance test id is a `def test_name(self)` method inside a unittest.TestCase subclass in the named file; no pytest fixtures; use the daemon test harness in tests/_harness.py.
1. Stale: daemon.stale_check(task) delegates to stale.evidence(task, graph_links=stale.load_links(), graph=interference.load_graph(), tasks=bus.read(role='execute')) and returns its dict (today's keys base, goal_head, moved_count, stale_paths, risk remain; signals/risk_reasons/graph added); _record_stale_check writes stale.row(...) with action recorded; _stale_rebase writes rows with action rebased/rebase_conflict; risk 'medium' is treated like 'low' for the stale_rebase decision (only high rebases).
2. merge.merge: on status merged, bus.update also sets merged_at=time.time() (top-level, mirrored into pipeline.merged_at when absent) and changed_files = git diff --name-only previous_sha..sha (bounded to 500 paths). scorecard.parallelism merge_wait_s must read either location (read stamp helper accepts pipeline or top-level; already does per _stamp — verify with a test).
3. executor.post_tool_result(replace_result=True): pop pipeline keys gated_at, gated_at_lease, gated_at_done and hold_reason/resume_hint gate residue, so gate() re-runs on the new head; record pipeline.regated_by='codex_reply'.
4. executor.start: inside the existing `else` branch that runs when no executor_id was supplied (executor.py:270-274), immediately after scores = scorecard.scores(...) and before pool.pick_executor is used for the final pick, so a caller-supplied executor_id path is untouched and scores is always defined: if [jev.routing].mode == active: routing = jev_route.shadow_context(t, pool) and scores = jev_route.active_scores(t, pool, routing['eligible'], routing['classification'], routing['evidence'], scores). Then if [allocation].mode != off: build the ranking inputs from the bus inside executor.start (no daemon import, daemon imports executor): graph = {x['id']: x for x in bus.read(role='execute', compact=False) if not x.get('merged_into') and x.get('status') != 'failed'} plus the task itself; durations = duration.durations_for(list(graph.values())); ready_ids = [x['id'] for x in graph.values() if x['status'] in ('queued', 'running') and bus.ready(x)] with the task id included; priority = critical_path.explain(t['id'], graph, durations); ready_priorities = [critical_path.explain(i, graph, durations)['critical_path_s'] for i in ready_ids]; eligible_ids = [e.id for e in pool.eligible_executors('execute', t['complexity'], t)]; ev = allocation.evidence_for(eligible_ids, scorecard.task_class(t)); baseline = pool.pick_executor('execute', t['complexity'], scores=scores, task=t); choice = allocation.choose(t, eligible_ids, baseline=baseline.id, priority=priority, ready_priorities=ready_priorities, evidence=ev); allocation.record(t['id'], choice); in active mode ex = pool.executors[choice['executor']], in shadow ex stays baseline. Any exception in these hooks -> baseline pick, hook error text stored in the run row (bus.log_run field allocation_error) and dispatch continues.
5. mcp.spawn_scout(task_id): before _bg, check = scout_evidence.reuse_check(task spec, objective=constraints.objective, head_sha=HEAD); scout_evidence.record_decision(...); when check['sufficient'] and constraints.force is not true, return {'task': id, 'status': 'skipped: reusable evidence', 'hits': check['hits']} and post the task result as done with result = {'summary': 'reused evidence: ' + ', '.join(hit ids), 'findings': [{'finding': hit['title'], 'source': hit['id'], 'confidence': 0.8, 'relevance': 'reused', 'unresolved': ''} for each fresh hit] (the shape scout_evidence.normalize_findings accepts), 'reused_evidence': check['hits'], 'provenance': ['repo']}; otherwise spawn as today.
Safety: security review path and reviews_expected untouched; allocation never returns an ineligible executor; all hooks fail open to today's behaviour.
acceptance: tests/test_daemon.py::test_stale_check_returns_extended_evidence_and_only_high_rebases — stale_check output has signals and risk_reasons; a medium risk never triggers _stale_rebase
tests/test_merge.py::test_merge_stamps_merged_at_and_changed_files — a successful merge leaves merged_at and a changed_files list on the task
tests/test_executor.py::test_reply_result_clears_gate_stamps_for_regating — post_tool_result with replace_result removes gated_at keys and sets regated_by

tests/test_executor.py::test_start_uses_allocation_only_in_active_mode_and_fails_open — with two concurrently ready execute tasks of different critical-path length on the bus, shadow mode keeps the baseline executor and writes an allocation decision row whose candidates carry non_critical_factor for the shorter task; active mode uses the chosen eligible executor for the critical one; a raising allocation.choose falls back to baseline and records allocation_error

tests/test_executor.py::test_start_applies_active_jev_scores_only_when_mode_active — with [jev.routing].mode active the scores passed to pick_executor are the adjusted ones; in shadow they are unchanged

tests/test_mcp.py::test_spawn_scout_skips_when_reusable_evidence_is_sufficient — sufficient fresh evidence returns skipped with hits and posts a done result whose findings each carry finding, source, confidence and relevance (normalize_findings keeps them all) plus reused_evidence; force true spawns anyway
tests/test_executor.py::test_start_with_explicit_executor_id_skips_routing_hooks — start(task, prompt, executor_id='sol') never calls jev_route or allocation and uses the given executor

constraints.interface_contract: stale_check(task) keeps today's keys and adds signals, risk_reasons, graph; merge() stamps merged_at and changed_files; post_tool_result(replace_result=True) clears gated_at*; executor.start hooks read [allocation].mode and [jev.routing].mode; spawn_scout returns status 'skipped: reusable evidence' when sufficient
